newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico annuls first auction for scenic railroad.
newsitem.headline: Mexico annuls first auction for scenic railroad.

text.p: Mexican officials Wednesday put off the privatisation of the scenic Chihuahua-Pacific railroad, long a favourite with tourists, after only one bidder at a concession auction turned in a price deemed too low.
The Chihuahua-Pacific line, which was to be the first of the country's rails to be sold off, meanders through Mexico's scenic Copper Canyon, a gorge as big as the Grand Canyon in the United States.

Mexico's Communications and Transport Ministry declared the auction null and void after Mexican mining firm Grupo Mexico offered to pay 201.79 million pesos ($27 million) for the 50-year concession -- well below the 376 million pesos ($49 million) estimated by officals as the value of the railway.
"By not meeting the minimum conditions, we have proposed declaring the auction of the Chihuahua-Pacific rail null and void," Assistant Secretary for Transport Aaron Dickter told a news conference.

Officials said they would consider selling the line as part of the concession to operate the Northeast line, the second part of the country's railroad privatisation, on Nov. 29. That line runs from Mexico City to Laredo, Texas, and is considered the crown jewel of all the railroads.
"We have to decide whether to hold another auction for the Chihuahua-Pacific rail line, or include it in the Northwest line," Dickter said.
Grupo Mexico had said it would be willing to invest 120 million pesos ($16 million) in the Chihuahua-Pacific railroad if it won the concession.

Mexico originally planned to sell its railroads during 1995 but was held up by bureaucratic problems. Its planned sell-off of its secondary petrochemicals industry has also snagged on political problems.
